issues.t: Crankshaft position sensor can crack and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, will not restart, or starts only after cooling down, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor housing could crack, so the engine computer loses the signal it needs to run the engine. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: A stall in traffic is dangerous, so do not wait. Check your VIN for recall 03V-030 and have the sensor replaced.

issues.t: Rear trailing arms rust and can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from the rear over bumps, the rear end feeling loose or wandering, or heavy rust visible on the arms ahead of the rear wheels.
issues.why: In states that use road salt, the rear trailing arms could corrode until they weaken and fracture, which affects how the rear wheels stay in place. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected right away and do not drive if the arms are badly rusted. Check your VIN for recall 09V-123.

issues.t: Front coil springs rust and snap (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from a front corner, the SUV sitting lower on one side, or a tire that suddenly goes flat.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the front coil springs until one breaks. A broken spring end can rub or cut into the tire. Hyundai recalled SUVs sold or registered in salt-belt states.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the front suspension checked if you hear a bang or the SUV leans. Check your VIN for recall 14V-435, which covers inspection and spring replacement.

issues.t: ABS kicks in at low speed and lengthens stops (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses or buzzes during gentle, slow stops on dry pavement and the SUV takes longer than expected to stop.
issues.why: Electrical noise in a wheel speed sensor signal could make the anti-lock system think a wheel is locking when it is not, so it eases off the brakes. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Leave extra stopping distance and get it fixed soon. Check your VIN for recall 04V-131.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor may treat a child as an adult (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light shows the airbag as on when a small child or child seat is in the front seat.
issues.why: The seat's occupant classification system could misjudge a small child as an adult, leaving the front passenger airbag active when it should be off. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs twice.
issues.next: Keep children in the back seat. Check your VIN for recalls 05V-450 and 05V-527 and have the system recalibrated.

issues.t: Fuel tank may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the rear of the SUV or fuel drips or wet spots under the tank.
issues.why: An internal baffle wall in the fuel tank could be made below specification, which could let the tank leak. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Do not drive or park indoors if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for recall 06V-317.

issues.t: ABS module can short from moisture (recall)
issues.sym: The ABS or brake warning light comes on, or anti-lock braking stops working.
issues.why: Moisture could get inside the anti-lock brake control module and cause an electrical short. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-061 and get it repaired soon. If you ever smell burning from the engine bay, park outside and away from buildings until a dealer looks at it.

issues.t: Brake light switch fails (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights that stay off or stay on, the shifter stuck in Park, cruise control not working, or stability control and check engine lights.
issues.why: The stop lamp switch near the brake pedal can wear or lose contact. That switch also tells the shift lock and other systems when the brakes are pressed. Hyundai recalled the 2007 models and later the 2007-2011 models.
issues.next: Drivers behind you may not see you braking, so get this fixed promptly. Check your VIN for recalls 09V-122 and 13V-113.

issues.t: Driver airbag clock spring can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: The clock spring is the coiled wiring inside the steering column that connects the driver airbag. It could break, so the airbag might not deploy in a crash. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 11V-472 and have the clock spring replaced. Never ignore an airbag light.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensing needs recalibration (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light shows when a small adult is sitting in the front seat.
issues.why: The occupant classification system under the passenger seat could fail to recognize a small adult and turn the passenger airbag off. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs for recalibration.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 12V-354 and have the system recalibrated by a dealer.

issues.t: Trailer hitch wiring module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke, a burning smell or melted wiring near the rear of the SUV, even when it is parked, or trailer lights acting up.
issues.why: The trailer wiring module used with the tow package could let in moisture or suffer an internal short, which can overheat and start a fire. Hyundai recalled 2007-2008 and 2009-2011 SUVs with these harnesses.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 08E-055 and 11E-040. Until the repair is done, park outside and unplug the trailer harness.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong from failed level sensors
issues.sym: The fuel gauge drops to empty right after filling, sticks at one level or jumps around, often with the check engine light on.
issues.why: These models use two fuel level sensors inside the tank, and their sensing contacts wear out. The engine computer then sees a bad reading and sets a fault code.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups so you do not run out of gas. A shop can confirm the code and replace the sensors; doing both at once is common because the job requires removing the rear seat.

issues.t: Misaligned intermediate shaft can wear the transmission (recall)
issues.sym: A grinding or whining noise from the transmission area, then a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: An intermediate shaft could be installed out of alignment, which wears the transmission internally until it stops sending power to the wheels. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Do not keep driving with a new grinding noise. Check your VIN for recall 11V-261.

issues.t: Rear brake calipers can leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, the brake warning light, or fluid wetness on the inside of a rear wheel.
issues.why: Some rear brake calipers were not machined correctly and could leak brake fluid, which reduces braking power. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Do not drive with a soft pedal or brake warning light. Check your VIN for recall 10V-613.

issues.t: Rod bearing wear on the 2.4L four-cylinder
issues.sym: A knock from the engine that gets faster as you rev it, the oil light, loss of power or stalling.
issues.why: Connecting rod bearings in this engine can wear early and lead to engine seizure. The 2012 models were recalled, and 2010-2012 models were added to an engine settlement with knock-detection software and longer warranty coverage for bearing damage.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear a knock. Have a Hyundai dealer check your VIN for recall 20V-746 and the knock-detection software update, which must be done before a failure to keep the extended coverage.

issues.t: Engine bearing failure and seizure
issues.sym: A knock that rises with engine speed, the check engine or oil light, the engine dropping into reduced power, or stalling.
issues.why: Machining debris or crankshaft surface flaws can starve the connecting rod bearings of oil until they wear and the engine seizes. Hyundai recalled the 2013-2014 Santa Fe Sport (recall 17V-226) and added knock-detection software with lifetime short-block coverage for 2013-2018 Santa Fe Sport and some early 2019 models.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear knocking. Check your VIN for recall 17V-226 and make sure the knock-detection software update has been done.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pipe may leak after engine repair (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell from the engine bay, especially after an engine was replaced under an earlier recall.
issues.why: On engines that were repaired or replaced under the bearing recalls, the high-pressure fuel pipe may not have been properly reinstalled and could leak fuel onto a hot engine. Hyundai recalled these SUVs.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel under the hood. Check your VIN for recall 18V-934.

issues.t: ABS control module fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, sometimes with the ABS light on, and it can happen while the SUV is parked and off.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control unit can develop an internal short. Recalls cover the 2013-2018 Santa Fe Sport, the 2016-2018 three-row Santa Fe, and the 2019 Santa Fe XL; the fix is a lower-rated fuse and module replacement if needed.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recalls 23V-651 and 22V-056. Park outdoors and away from buildings until a dealer completes the repair.

issues.t: Right front axle shaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: A loud clunk, then the engine revs but the SUV does not move, or it rolls when left in Park.
issues.why: The right front axle shaft could fracture, cutting power to the wheels. Without the parking brake set, a parked SUV could roll away. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for recall 13V-355.

issues.t: Hood latch can rust and let the hood fly open (recall)
issues.sym: The hood pops up while driving, does not close firmly, or the release feels stiff or sticky.
issues.why: The cable for the secondary hood latch can corrode and bind, so the latch does not hold the hood if the main latch lets go. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: If the hood will not latch firmly, do not drive. Check your VIN for recall 17V-358.

issues.t: Seat belt warning may not work (recall)
issues.sym: No seat belt reminder chime or light when someone is unbuckled.
issues.why: Wiring to the seat belt buckle could be damaged during assembly, so the system cannot tell whether the belt is fastened. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-145 and make sure everyone buckles up in the meantime.
issues.sevReason: Seat belt reminder warning only; the belt itself works.

issues.t: Steering wheel may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Play or a clunk in the steering wheel itself, or the wheel feeling loose on the column.
issues.why: The steering wheel could crack or separate from the steering column, causing loss of steering control. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Do not drive if the steering wheel feels loose. Check your VIN for recall 18V-118.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags can be damaged when they deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: The mounting bolts for the side curtain airbags could cut into the airbags as they inflate, reducing protection in a crash. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-715 and have the dealer complete it.

issues.t: Oil consumption on the 2.4L direct-injection engine
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, the oil light comes on, or the engine smokes or loses power when oil gets low.
issues.why: Carbon can build up in the piston oil control rings on this engine, and a clogged PCV valve can make it worse, so the engine burns oil. Running low on oil can damage the bearings.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up or two and top off as needed. Ask a dealer about Hyundai's oil consumption bulletin and the knock-detection update, and keep oil change receipts for warranty claims.

issues.t: Tow hitch wiring module fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the rear of the SUV, sometimes when it is parked and off.
issues.why: Water can reach the circuit board in the trailer hitch wiring module and short it out. The module has constant power, so it can overheat even with the SUV off. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs, including hybrids and plug-in hybrids.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 23V-181. Park outside and away from buildings until new wiring and a fuse are installed.

issues.t: Fuel line connection may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell from under the hood or wet fuel near the engine.
issues.why: A fuel pipe connection on the engine might not have been tightened or seated properly at the factory and can leak, which raises the risk of fire. Hyundai issued two recalls.
issues.next: Do not drive or park indoors if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for recalls 21V-308 and 21V-524.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not switch off for a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light shows on with a child seat in the front seat.
issues.why: The occupant detection module might not recognize a rear-facing child seat, so the front passenger airbag stays armed. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Put child seats in the back seat. Check your VIN for recall 21V-185.

issues.t: Transmission oil pump fault can cause power loss (recall)
issues.sym: A transmission warning, the SUV dropping into limp mode, or a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: The transmission's oil pump can malfunction, and the backup limp mode may not work as intended, so the SUV can lose power. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Get to a safe spot if a transmission warning appears. Check your VIN for recall 22V-746 and have it repaired before regular driving.

issues.t: Turbo oil supply pipe can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front, a burning oil smell, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The pipe that feeds oil to the turbocharger can crack and spray oil in the engine bay, which can cause a fire or starve the turbo of oil. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Stop and shut off the engine if you see smoke. Check your VIN for recall 22V-197.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: A blank or frozen screen when shifting into Reverse.
issues.why: A circuit board in the camera system can be damaged so the backup image does not display. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Use your mirrors and look behind you when backing up. Check your VIN for recall 24V-879.

issues.t: SUV may roll away in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV creeps or moves after you shift into Park and get out.
issues.why: A software error in the transmission control could keep the transmission from properly locking in Park. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs for a software update.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for recall 24V-529 and get the update.

issues.t: Floor wiring can chafe and affect airbags (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: A wiring harness under the floor could rub against a nearby part until it is damaged, which could make airbags deploy unexpectedly or not deploy in a crash. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Do not ignore an airbag light. Check your VIN for recall 24V-561.

issues.t: Backup camera image missing or blocked (recall)
issues.sym: No camera picture in Reverse, or a trailer parking message covering the backup image.
issues.why: Damage to the camera wiring harness can cut out the image, and on 2024 models a trailer parking assist message could cover the camera view. Hyundai issued recalls for both.
issues.next: Look behind you and use mirrors when reversing. Check your VIN for recalls 25V-808 and 24V-246.

issues.t: Starter terminal cover can let the starter short (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine area, or the engine not cranking.
issues.why: The protective cover on the starter motor's power terminal may not be installed properly, so the terminal can short against nearby metal and overheat. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-659. If you smell burning, shut the SUV off and park it outside.

issues.t: Connecting rod bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the engine, an oil leak, warning lights or a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: Bolts holding the connecting rods might not have been tightened correctly at the factory, which can damage the engine. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine starts knocking. Check your VIN for recall 25V-549.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: The side curtain airbags may not have been installed correctly, so they might not protect occupants as designed in a crash. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-809 and have the dealer inspect it.

issues.t: Front seat belt anchors may detach (recall)
issues.sym: A front seat belt that feels loose at its lower mounting point, or a rattle near the base of a front seat.
issues.why: The anchor holding the driver or passenger seat belt may not be secured properly and could come loose in a crash. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-218 and have the anchors inspected promptly.

issues.t: Instrument panel display may go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The digital gauge cluster goes dark, so speed and warning lights are not shown.
issues.why: A software error can cause the instrument panel display to stop working. Hyundai recalled affected SUVs for a software update.
issues.next: Pull over safely if the gauges go blank. Check your VIN for recall 26V-047 and get the update.

issues.t: Tire information label does not meet the standard (recall 03V-520)
issues.sym: The sticker in the door opening does not give the tire and load information in the required form.
issues.why: The labels printed for these years did not match the federal labelling rule, so owners can set tire pressures from wrong information.
issues.next: Get the corrected label from a dealer and set the tires to the pressures it lists.

issues.t: Windshield may not be glued in properly (recall 21V-00M)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a water leak at the top of the windshield, or glass that looks slightly out of place.
issues.why: The windshield may have been bonded without the proper adhesive, so it can come out of the opening in a crash.
issues.next: Have a dealer remove and reinstall the windshield under the recall; it is free and it matters for crash protection.

issues.t: Crankshaft surface defect can wear the V6 bearings (recall 17V-578)
issues.sym: A knock or rumble from deep in the engine, oil pressure or engine warning lights, and in bad cases the engine stalls and will not restart.
issues.why: Machining marks on the crankshaft let the connecting rod bearings wear quickly, which starves them of oil film and damages the engine.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and the engine inspected; Hyundai replaces damaged engines free under the recall. Stop driving if the engine knocks.

issues.t: Front suspension and wheel bearing wear
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles over bumps, a hum or growl from one wheel that gets louder with speed, steering that feels loose or wanders, and tires wearing unevenly.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs, ball joints, tie rod ends and the sway bar links and bushings on this generation wear out sooner than owners expect, and road salt speeds the wear up.
issues.next: Have a shop check the front end and spin each wheel bearing. Worn joints and bearings become a safety problem once they are loose, so do not put the repair off.
